sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Internet Retailing of Outdoor Sports and Camping Gear

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Franco-Napoleonic tradition, subject to EU supranational law and Luxembourg commercial law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–Germany Double Taxation and Tax Treaty (DTA/DTAA, as amended)
BLEU–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (under the Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union, with 2005 revision applicable to Luxembourg)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the Fight against Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AML/CFT Law), as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Loi du 13 janvier 2019 portant création d'un registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 September 2019 on RBE registration; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies and on annual accounts; CSSF Regulation No. 16-08 of 12 May 2016 and CSSF Circulars 19/732 and 21/788 on AML/CFT.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of legal existence / good standing and articles of association of each non-Luxembourg corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial or company registry in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Hague Convention countries; otherwise Consular Legalization at a Luxembourg diplomatic/consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney / proxy executed by each shareholder, director, or legal representative for the Luxembourg incorporation notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent authority in the country where the power is signed; corporate signatories must attach a board resolution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, unless executed before the Luxembourg notary directly

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized/certified copy of proof of identity and residence for each UBO and director (passport, recent bank or utility statement, and if applicable a police certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport/civil registry authority, police clearance authority in the country of origin, and the certifying notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization only if required for official public certificates; otherwise notarized copies accepted

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding screening of every UBO, director, and authorized officer against (i) the EU Financial Sanctions/European regulation lists, (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the US OFAC SDN list, and (iv) the Luxembourg and EU PEP referential database. Positive matches require enhanced due diligence, escalation to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier – CRF), and refusal of incorporation if sanctions apply under applicable law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online portal at lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be composed using the Latin alphabet and may include Luxembourgish, French, or German words. Non-Latin script content is not accepted by the RCS as the operative legal name; a standardized Romanized transliteration must be filed and will be used in all RCS registrations. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS entry and must contain sufficient distinctive element as required by Article 15 of the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An RCS name reservation may be extended by filing a renewal request through the LBR portal during the final 10 days of the initial 30-day window, for one additional 30-day period. If the RCS registrar rejects the name, the applicant may (i) submit a revised name using a new distinctive element; (ii) file a written complaint against the registrar's refusal through LBR; and (iii) bring a judicial appeal before the Commercial Chamber of the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg within one month of refusal notification, with mandatory legal representation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for a low-risk online retail business only if a licensed domiciliation agent/fiduciary maintains a physical registered address in Luxembourg, accepts service of process, and keeps all corporate and accounting records available in Luxembourg. A mere PO Box or mail-forward-only virtual office is not acceptable for SARL incorporation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Less than 5% annual first-year risk for a low-risk e-commerce ISIC 4791 business with proper registered office and record-keeping; risk increases if RBE filings are incomplete or statutory accounting records are not producible at the registered office within statutory time limits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCS fee schedule for name reservation and negative certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff applicable to minimum-capital SARL incorporations (approx. EUR 1,300–1,600)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary VAT at 17% on incorporation deed fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Luxembourg VAT rate of 17% on notarial fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official translation of foreign corporate documents into French and/or German
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for certified translation of statutes, certificates, and powers of attorney (3–5 pages)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of parent-company and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Apostille authorities in document origin countries; Luxembourg consular posts for non-Hague states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Estimated per-document fee for a four-document UBO/corporate package from typical Hague jurisdictions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Domiciliation / registered office service for SARL (first year, inclusive of registered agent duties)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Standard Luxembourg market rate for low-risk retail SARL with a physical service address and RBE record-keeping
Official RCS filing schedule for SARL incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RESA publication fee for company incorporation notice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial Owner Register (RBE) filing and initial compliance record setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg domiciliation agent / RCS RBE service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Professional service fee for UBO declaration and AML/CFT file preparation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation PEP, UN, EU, and OFAC sanctions screening and KYC verification bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance service provider / local AML counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-scope screening fee covering UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat professional preparation fee for a standard e-commerce KYC/onboarding package

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 1, 9, 22, 25, 26, 100-109 governing SARL formation, share capital, and registration); Civil Code Articles 1832 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), managed by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Charter of Incorporation (Statuts de Société) and the Application for Registration (Formulaire de demande d'immatriculation au RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum issued share capital of EUR 12,000; share capital must be fully subscribed and paid up before incorporation and may be credited to an escrow account of a Luxembourg bank or notary
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the subscribers of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée adopt the Articles of Association in the form presented. RESOLVED: That the paid-up share capital is subscribed as set forth and shall be deposited with a Luxembourg credit institution. RESOLVED: That the registered office of the company is established at [address], in the City of Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED: That the company is declared and registered under the corporate name provided in the Articles. RESOLVED: That [Name] is appointed Manager (Gérant), with full powers to represent the company and to carry out all registration formalities, including signing of all filings before the RCS and publication formalities. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the Managers open the company bank account and execute all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute the Articles of Association and Capital Subscription Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire public) for authentic deed; subsequently the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each subscriber must appear before a Luxembourg notary to execute the notarial deed of incorporation containing the Articles of Association. Duly identify all subscribers and verify share subscription, minimum capital contribution of EUR 12,000, and appointment of the SARL manager. The notary will obtain a certificate of non-conflict of corporate name and will collect the signed capital blockages or bank certificate. After execution, instruct the notary to submit the e-form and request an RCS registration number.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association (Statuts)
Bank certificate or escrow certificate evidencing payment of subscribed share capital
Subscriber identification documents (passport or national ID)
Statement of capacity of signatories and list of subscribers
Certificate of non-conflict of corporate name (obtained beforehand by notary)
Manager's domicile proof and authorization to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or RCS queries the application, the deficit must be cured by filing an amending deed or providing supplementary declarations. Any missing document may be re-submitted via the Luxembourg Business Registers portal; a rejection due to insufficient capital requires a corrected capital certificate before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Registration and Obtain the RCS Registration Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) e-file platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or a designated authorized person submits the electronic registration application (e-form) to the RCS, including the authenticated deed and the Articles. Verify registration data against the official RCS extract. Upon acceptance, the RCS issues the registration number and legal entity status, and publishes the incorporation notice in the Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
required_dossiers: Completed RCS registration e-form signed by the manager
Notarial deed of incorporation
Copy of the bank certificate of capital contribution
Domicile/office lease or evidence of registered office availability
Identification of the manager (Gérant)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: An RCS refusal or delay is cured by correcting formal defects within the online workspace, re-uploading the deed, and paying any supplemental fee. If the company name conflicts, a new name must be reserved and the notarial deed amended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Mandatory Legal Notices and Notify Tax, Social Security, and Statistical Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA); Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes); Social Security Centre (Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale - CCSS); Luxembourg Statistical Office (STATEC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: RCS publishes the notice automatically. After receiving the RCS number, file the existence of the company with the direct tax administration (declaration of existence) and register with the social security center for employer obligations. STATEC registration occurs during tax registration and when the company records its start of business.
required_dossiers: Copy of the RCS registration extract
Manager's identification form (form 760 or equivalent employee declaration for the manager)
Company registered-office address and contact details
Lease or title of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social security registration is delayed, submit a manual request to the relevant service with the RCS extract and identification proofs. For CCSS, apply for late correction of the start date and pay any assessed social charges; for STATEC, verify that the activity code 4791 is entered correctly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Implement Corporate Governance, Accounts Framework and Bank Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company manager and shareholders; Luxembourg bank for account opening; Luxembourg Inland Revenue for annual accounts filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Implement the initial internal records and governance framework: adopt internal rules, open the commercial bank account, execute payment rails (Stripe/PayPal) with KYC documents. Appoint an independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) if the SARL exceeds two of the following thresholds: balance sheet total of EUR 4.4 million, net turnover of EUR 8.8 million, or 50 full-time employees. Ensure accounting records are maintained and prepare for the annual accounts filing.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Bylaws and Manager's identification
Bank account opening forms and ultimate beneficial ownership declaration
Before any financing or authorization, the agreed payment service provider documents (Stripe/PayPal) for KYC and business description
Signed board resolution appointing manager and auditor where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment processor rejects the corporate application, supply a certified copy of the RCS registration, beneficial ownership statement, and amended description of the outdoor camping equipment retail activity. Correct any mismatch in business purpose description; if the auditor requirement applies, appoint and file the appointment with the RCS.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for an internet retailing activity of outdoor camping equipment (ISIC 4791); no industrial establishment to be licensed
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific operating or manufacturing permit required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency (Administration de l'environnement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category null or Commercial activities without physical industrial installation; no EIA required for pure e-commerce warehousing/retail
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste thresholds triggered; commercial e-commerce operations must comply with general waste segregation and packaging obligations under Luxembourg waste law

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Standard workplace compliance under the Multilateral Agreement on Safety and Health at Work: fire safety certification for any occupied office/warehouse premises, building structural load acceptance certificate or lease compliance confirmation, and occupational safety clearance from the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (Inspection du travail et des mines - ITM)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration) for direct taxes, and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT/GST; electronic filing and registrations are processed through MyGuichet.lu and the Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE) portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity with Luxembourg VAT obligations must first obtain a Luxembourg corporate or VAT identification number. For EU-established entities, registration may be completed directly via MyGuichet.lu using the standard VAT registration form and legalized or apostilled corporate documents, accompanied by evidence of economic activity in Luxembourg. Non-EU entities must appoint an approved Luxembourg tax representative who is jointly liable for VAT. The application requires the foreign entity's constitutive documents, proof of identity of directors, and registration certificate from the home jurisdiction. After validation, the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number and confirms the direct tax registration obligation for any Luxembourg permanent establishment or resident SARL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Luxembourg SARL is classified as a fully taxable corporate entity and cannot elect pass-through treatment; no check-the-box regime is available. Luxembourg has transposed the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive (ATAD), and limited elections may be made for hybrid mismatches and tax-timing alignment. For VAT purposes, qualifying taxable persons may elect to form a VAT group and may opt for simplified accounting schemes where permitted by the Luxembourg VAT authorities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) implemented under the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies to taxable persons established in Luxembourg; every person making taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register for VAT. Non-established EU suppliers of distance sales of goods are subject to the EU-wide EUR 10,000 annual distance-sales threshold, above which Luxembourg VAT registration or the One Stop Shop (OSS) becomes mandatory. A small-business exemption applies to domestic Luxembourg taxable persons with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000, but business registration and compliance obligations must still be met before claiming the exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance system, digital stamping mandate, or continuous transaction controls for VAT. Mandatory electronic invoicing is limited to invoices issued to Luxembourg public-sector entities, which must be transmitted through the national B2G e-invoicing platform. B2B e-invoicing is optional. Periodic VAT returns and recapitulative statements must be filed electronically, and SAF-T files may be required from certain taxpayers during audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to supplies of goods physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by or on behalf of the supplier, provided the supplier retains documentary evidence of export. Intangible services related to exports and certain auxiliary transport services may also qualify for zero-rating. Intra-EU B2B supplies are zero-rated only when the customer holds a valid VAT identification number, the goods are transported to another Member State, and the supply is correctly disclosed in the recapitulative statement. For challenges see: Use of OSS for distance sales is mandatory above EUR 10,000, where the supply is instead taxed in the destination Member State.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / EX-A and stamped export certificate)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR transport document proving physical removal from the EU
Commercial invoice issued in the name of the foreign customer
Packing list and warehouse dispatch evidence
Proof of payment or bank transfer from the foreign customer (including inward remittance evidence)
Luxembourg VAT return and recapitulative statement disclosing the zero-rated supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If a taxpayer fails to substantiate a zero-rated export or submits false or incomplete documentation, the Luxembourg VAT authorities may retrospectively reassess the supply at the standard 17% rate. Default interest applies from the due date of the original VAT return, together with fines up to EUR 10,000 for negligence and substantially higher penalties for intentional fraud. Criminal sanctions, including imprisonment, may apply in cases of fraudulent export schemes. The appointed tax representative can be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid VAT, interest, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Luxembourg franc has been fully replaced by the euro (EUR); Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls or restrictions on either current account or capital account transactions. Profit remittances, liquidation proceeds, loan repayments, and royalty distributions are freely transferable cross-border to/from non-residents. Local banks require a valid economic substance rationale and AML/KYC documentation for every wire, and the BCL collects statistical Balance of Payments reporting for payments above EUR 12,500; this is not an authorization requirement. There are no surrender or conversion thresholds against EUR.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds or to repatriate foreign currency earnings to Luxembourg. Exporters may hold retained receipts in EUR or foreign currency in offshore accounts, provided the transactions are truthfully recorded in Luxembourg financial statements and tax returns. No mandatory conversion ratio or timeline applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte Séquestre) and Operational EUR/USD Settlement Account
Commercial Operational Account and Forex Pre-Advice Account
Operational Cash Management Account (CAC) and Capital Contribution Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Cross-Border Trade Settlement Account and Nostro Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium - EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Wise/Lunar are legally allowed to issue payment accounts under CSSF PSD2; however, for Stage 4 the EUR clearing rails for high-volume online camping gear retail should rely on a Luxembourg licensed payment institution or an NCCB with access to TARGET2. EMIs are viable for low-value subscriptions and payouts to suppliers under a segregated safeguarding framework (missing pass-through / MT103 direct participant), but they cannot serve as a substitute for a primary credit institution's capital escrow account. Any Dark Pool-like settlement arrangement is prohibited unless registered under the Payment Services Law of 10 November 2009.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not impose a rigid physical-presence requirement for every SARL director, but CSSF Circular CSSF 12/552 and AML Law of 12 November 2004 require all beneficial owners to be positively identified. In practice, Tier 1 banks mandate at least one physical interview of the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one authorized signatory at the bank's premises or before a Luxembourg notary; fully remote onboarding is exceptionally tolerated for existing CSSF regulated clients or when identity is verified via a qualified remote onboarding portal certified by CSSF, with apostilled/certified copy robust diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder structure includes offshore tax havens or trusts with opaque UBOs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart listing every 25%+ shareholder; certified copies of passports; tax residency certificates for each ultimate UBO; declaration of source of funds backed by dividend vouchers or the equivalent; bank reference letter from an EU bank; notarized corporate resolution in French or English.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SARL has a non-EU director or PSTC (Produit et Service au Compte de Tiers) activity performing cross-border treasury instructions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid residence permit; anti-money laundering awareness certificate; power of attorney / procuration notarized and legalized by consulate; passport copy; biometric indicia; liability insurance certificate; data protection registration with CNPD.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High monthly flows of internet retail proceeds from Stripe/PayPal into a single operational account without explained transactional nature
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: E-commerce platform licence/reconciliation ledger; Stripe/PayPal merchant agreement; historical transaction volume report for six months; fulfilment contracts with suppliers; payment gateway contract clauses showing delivery (FOB or DAP); sample invoices (AM-001/2025) and corresponding customs declarations for cross-border EU dispatch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment service provider (PSP) settlement currencies mismatch in EUR/local currency cause a high volume of reversed or returned FX closed-loop payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Currency conversion policies from PSPs; FX rate sheets; treasury hedging agreement (FX Forward / NDF) with a Luxembourg Tier 1 bank; daily sweep protocol; reconciliation framework for currency conversion fees and interchange.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the Luxembourg SARL are transmitted via SWIFT MT103 (customer transfer) or MT202 (bank-to-bank / bankwise, only for the bank itself). For investment capital, the remittance instruction must include the purpose code 'Capital Injection under Articles 183-1 of Luxembourg Companies Law' and, if the contribution is made by a non-resident corporate shareholder, a written equity contribution resolution in English/French. The receiving Luxembourg bank will not require conversion of USD/GBP/CHF into EUR; however, it will report the receipt to BCL under the Balance of Payments statistical code 'F DI 1 - Equity capital / jezuity', and no exchange premium applies because the euro is the legal tender. No prior ministerial authorization is required, unless the corporate activity involves a regulated sector (not applicable for internet retailing of outdoor camping equipment).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements for trade settlement should use the following rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for unencumbered supplier wires, with instruction field 70 noting 'PURCHASE OF GOODS - OUTDOOR CAMPING EQUIPMENT' and the final invoice number; (2) SWIFT MT202 for correspondent bank to bank clearing where no beneficiary customer details are disclosed; (3) SWIFT MT700 / MT710 for Irrevocable Documentary Loans or Commercial Letters of Credit when the supplier requires deferred payment security; (4) SEPA CT and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for all euro-denominated EEA trade payments below EUR 100,000; and (5) commercial documentary collections (DP/DA) via the collecting bank in the supplier's country. For all outbound USD moves, follow OFAC/embargo screening and Luxembourgische SDN filtering obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards on EUR, USD, GBP, CNY and CHF
FX Options (plain vanilla European style, calls/puts)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for tenors > 12 months
NDFs (non-deliverable forwards) for restricted currencies such as CNY, INR or BRL, subject to internal hedge effectiveness documentation
FX swaps (swap foreign exchange, sometimes known as BBE4)
Cross-currency basis swap under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement by Luxembourg credit institutions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders' approval of annual accounts at the ordinary general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Sàrl shareholders; signed minutes retained in the corporate Minute Book; no government filing required at meeting date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL the ordinary general meeting must be held by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No immediate RCS penalty for the meeting itself, but failure to approve accounts blocks the statutory filing with the RCS; continuing default exposes managers to liability, court summons, and eventual judicial dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit and publication of annual accounts (abbreviated balance sheet permissible for small SARLs, management report, and auditor's report when applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), published in the RESA electronic compendium
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholders' approval and no later than 7 months after the balance-sheet date; calendar-year SARL must file by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS formal reminder followed by criminal fines from EUR 250 to EUR 25,000 on managers under Article 42 of the Law of 19 December 2002; non-filing for two consecutive financial years may trigger court-ordered dissolution at the request of the Public Prosecutor; personal liability of directors is also exposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO register reconfirmation (confirmed beneficial ownership declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (UBO Register), filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Reconfirmation must occur at least once every 12 months and before the anniversary of the last UBO declaration; any transfer of SARL shares that changes direct or indirect beneficial ownership must be updated within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missed reconfirmation triggers a formal notice from the register manager; intentionally false or incomplete UBO disclosures are criminal offences punishable by 3 months to 3 years' imprisonment and/or fines from EUR 2,500 to EUR 50,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax declaration and minimum net wealth tax payment (impôt sur la fortune — Luxembourg 'franchise-type' recurring corporate levy)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg direct tax administration, submitted via electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed jointly with the annual corporate income tax and municipal business tax return; standard deadline is 31 May of the following calendar year for a 31 December year-end, with electronic filing extensions available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the tax due plus statutory late-payment interest; risk of estimated assessment and enforced tax collection of the minimum net wealth tax demand (standard minimum EUR 3,500, with reduced minima for small entities); potential attachment of bank accounts or receivables.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a duly licensed independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) is required when the SARL exceeds at least two of the three size tests on the balance-sheet date: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average workforce above 50 employees. A SARL below these thresholds is exempt from statutory audit, unless shareholders holding at least 10% of the share capital petition the court for an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial registers and annual accounts, transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; small companies may file abbreviated annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU is available for consolidated financial statements in certain defined cases.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Law of 13 January 2019 on the register of beneficial owners and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 June 2022, every UBO entry must be reconfirmed electronically at least once per calendar year, no later than 12 months after the last confirmation. Reconfirmation certifies that the registered beneficial owners remain accurate; if a transfer of shares creates a new beneficial owner holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights, a corrected UBO declaration must be filed within 30 days of the transaction. The annual reconfirmation is a separate mandatory step and applies even where the SARL has no change of ownership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members — SARL register of nominative shares (registre des actions nominatives)
Register of Directors — RCS company file and internal record of current directors
Minute Book — minutes of shareholders' general meetings and management decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,600–3,300 (EUR 1,500–3,000) typical Luxembourg domiciliation and registered office service charge per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000–18,000 (EUR 4,500–16,500) typical market fee for a small-to-medium online retail SARL statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% national corporate income tax (IRC) plus a 7% solidarity surcharge on the IRC and municipal business tax at communal rates; aggregate effective headline in Luxembourg City approximately 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; targeted relief includes the participation exemption for qualifying intercorporate dividends and capital gains, an 80% exemption for qualifying IP-derived income (effective 5% IP box rate), R&D tax credits, and group reorganization / rollover relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 700 (Modèle 700/700C) - annual corporate income tax and municipal business tax return; filed electronically via the Luxembourg professional e-Space on myguichet.lu operated by the Administration des contributions directes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; fiscal year is typically the calendar year, though a different business year-end may be adopted upon prior notification.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within six months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, the filing deadline is 30 June of the following year. Extensions may be granted on justified application to the competent local tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal form (SARL), name, registered office, Luxembourg RCS number, business identification number, and trade register details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the SARL maintains a Luxembourg registered office and, where needed, a designated local tax representative. Non-resident shareholders do not enter their own identification here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting period: start and end dates of the fiscal year, normally 1 January to 31 December.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a newly incorporated SARL, enter the short accounting period from incorporation to the first year-end. Foreign-sourced income of the non-resident shareholder is not reportable in this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial result: net profit or loss before tax per the annual financial statements prepared in accordance with Luxembourg GAAP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the worldwide taxable profit of the Luxembourg tax-resident SARL. If the entity is a pure holding or finance vehicle, ensure the accounting result is reconciled with the functional financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: add-back of non-deductible expenses and deduction of exempt income, including the 80% IP exemption and participation exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border service, royalty, and management fees to related parties must be at arm's length and documented before entry. Non-deductible items include excessive compensation, fines, and non-arm's-length payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss schedule: brought-forward net operating losses and current-year offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Luxembourg permits indefinite carryforward, but the portion of taxable income exceeding EUR 10 million can be offset by losses up to 70% only. Loss history of the SARL only, not group losses, is entered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption election: exempt dividends and capital gains derived from qualifying shareholdings, and any foreign withholding tax credits recoverable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL must itself hold at least 10% or EUR 1.2 million of the participating interest and, where relevant, satisfy the 12-month holding requirement. Non-resident ultimate owners must not be entered as the participants.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax (communal trade tax): allocation of the taxable profit to the Luxembourg municipality in which the SARL has its registered office or permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an internet retailer with no physical Luxembourg logistics, office, or staff, assess whether any action creates a Luxembourg permanent establishment. If no PE exists, the municipal tax base may nonetheless be maintained at the registered office; clarify with the competent municipal tax officer.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers default assessment under the General Tax Law, late payment interest at 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum), and administrative fines. Fraudulent non-filing may lead to a surcharge of up to the full tax evaded and criminal fines; prolonged non-compliance permits distraint proceedings against bank accounts and other assets.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on distributions to non-resident shareholders; 0% under the domestic participation exemption where the parent holds at least 10% or EUR 1.2 million, for at least 12 months, and meets the anti-abuse requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced or zero treaty rate, the non-resident shareholder must deliver a valid foreign tax residence certificate (TRC) and a declaration of beneficial ownership to the Luxembourg paying agent before payment; the treaty rate is then applied at source. If tax has been over-withheld, the shareholder should file a refund claim with the Luxembourg tax administration attaching the TRC, dividend vouchers, and evidence of ownership and substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no source withholding tax on arm's-length royalties or ordinary interest paid to non-residents, irrespective of any treaty rate. The only exception is interest on profit-sharing bonds, subject to 15% domestic WHT, which may be reduced or exempted under an applicable double tax treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Luxembourg entity must prepare and retain a Local File when the ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue reaches EUR 750 million and the Luxembourg entity's aggregate related-party transactions exceed EUR 1.5 million per year; the Master File is required at the same group turnover threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulation code analogous to offshore financial centers; however, treaty access, the beneficial ownership rule, ATAD anti-abuse provisions, and Luxembourg jurisprudence require a SARL to demonstrate real substance: registered office, qualified directors, proportionate operational staff, board and management decisions, physical or virtual premises, and adequate records. An online retailer of outdoor camping gear must substantiate its e-commerce functions, inventory and logistics arrangements, contracting counterparts, payment rails, and day-to-day management held in Luxembourg if it wishes to secure tax residency and treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-declaration of online sales revenue processed through Stripe or PayPal, omission of cross-border e-commerce turnover, falsification of accounting books, fabrication of dormant status, or wasteful profit extraction through sham loans, inflated management fees, or fictitious invoices to related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the taxable base under the Luxembourg General Tax Law, late payment interest at 7.2% per annum, administrative penalties up to the full amount of the evaded tax, and criminal prosecution with fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of up to five years for tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns or commit fraudulent acts can be made jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt; criminal proceedings may result in asset freezes, travel bans, disqualification from managing any Luxembourg company, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Luxembourg SARL as a letterbox company with no genuine local activity, where all substantive management, sales, inventory, and personnel decisions are taken outside Luxembourg, and the entity is used solely to access Luxembourg treaty benefits and shelter e-commerce profits from foreign residence taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of Luxembourg tax residency and treaty benefits, anti-abuse recharacterization of the entity's transactions, retroactive assessment plus interest, administrative abuse-of-law penalties, and potential criminal sanctions for facilitating tax evasion by the foreign beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: De jure and de facto directors may be ordered to pay recharacterized tax liabilities where they have lent their identity to a sham structure; criminal courts may issue exit bans, seize personal assets, and impose custodial sentences for complicity in abusive arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register the ultimate beneficial owners of the SARL in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), non-filing or late filing of annual accounts, use of informal nominee shareholders without a compliant UBO declaration, or concealment of controlling ownership through artificial trust or holding chains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to EUR 125,000 per failure under Luxembourg laws implementing AML/UBO requirements; penalties may also include further orders by the Luxembourg financial regulator if the payment services are linked to Stripe or PayPal, and loss of eligibility for tax treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and persons failing to submit UBO declarations face personal fines and, in serious cases, criminal liability. They may be barred from holding corporate office, subjected to travel restrictions in connection with ongoing investigations, and held civilly liable for investor or creditor damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of non-arm's-length transfer prices for online retail flows, such as artificially low mark-up on a Luxembourg sales entity, unreasonable intercompany procurement commissions, undocument service fees paid to related entities, or recurring losses of the Luxembourg SARL while the group remains profitable, without contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment of the Luxembourg taxable base, possible secondary adjustment recharacterizing excess profits as a dividend subject to 15% dividend withholding tax, denial of deductibility of the related-party charges, late payment interest, and administrative penalties for failure to maintain or present transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who deliberately implement or approve a non-compliant cross-border pricing system may be personally assessed as joint debtors for resulting tax debts where they have acted outside the interest of the company and in violation of Luxembourg corporate law.
